review.material: MIT Press description and edition information read. The OCW-recommended Internet Archive route was checked, but interior book pages were not reviewed.
review.limitations: Publisher-description-only review. The 432-page book, its formal details, visual demonstrations and design applications were not examined directly. No empirical efficacy or computational-superiority finding is inferred.

sections.title: What the publisher says the book is about
sections.text: Stiny presents designing as calculation with shapes, emphasizing that ambiguity and changing ways of seeing can support creative work.

sections.title: The stated argument
sections.text: Rule-governed calculation need not be restricted to manipulating numbers or verbal symbols. According to the description, shapes support visual expression whose interpretation can change during design.

sections.title: Reported development
sections.text: The description outlines a progression from seeing versus counting, through formal shape calculation, to specific design examples. Drawings carry much of the exposition, so a text-only synopsis cannot replace reading them.

sections.title: What is not established by this review
sections.text: The publisher’s account identifies the argument; it does not independently validate it. The actual formal definitions, example derivations, implementation requirements and practical outcomes need inspection in the book.

sections.title: How to approach the original
sections.text: Compare what a drawing visibly contains with the particular objects used to describe it. In each illustrated rule application, ask whether a new interpretation becomes possible. Use the formal sections to check the exact permitted operations.
